transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I've been having some thoughts that are starting to scare me. Lately, I just catch myself thinking that it would be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes, especially on the drive home from school, I just wonder if my family and my students would be better off without me. I don't want to actually do anything, but just having those thoughts... it's why I knew I needed to come in.
Have you made a plan to end your life?

No, I haven't made a plan. Like I was just saying, I really don't want to actually act on these thoughts. I haven't thought about how I would do it or anything like that. It's really just those passive thoughts popping up about not waking up, or thinking my family and my students would be better off. I don't have any intention of doing anything to make that happen.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

I'm not really sure if it's most days. I haven't exactly been keeping track of it like that. I just know I've been feeling... well, just really drained lately, and then having those thoughts I mentioned. But I haven't really noticed if it's an everyday thing.
Did something stressful happen in your life around the time these thoughts started?

Well, yeah, actually. It started around a year and seven months ago. That was when I took on the STEM assessment redesign at school. I was already doing my regular teaching load, and then I added that on top of it. That's when all this really started.
If the extra STEM redesign work were taken away, do you think these thoughts and feelings would mostly go away?

I don't know. I mean, maybe? It's hard to say. The extra work definitely triggered all this, but at this point, I'm not sure if just taking it away would fix everything. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to my softball league, my book club, working in my garden... even the robotics club I help with at school. But lately, I mostly just go through the motions with all of it. Or I just end up canceling, because none of those things really feel enjoyable to me anymore.
How has your sleep been lately?

It hasn't been very good. I can be completely exhausted, but I'll just lie awake replaying assessment deadlines and, you know, classroom mistakes in my head. And then when I do fall asleep, I usually end up waking up around 4 a.m., and I never really get back to sleep after that.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

I wouldn't really say I feel sad. I mean... I haven't noticed feeling down in that specific way, like wanting to cry or anything. Like I said, I'm just exhausted and mostly going through the motions right now. But... no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, I really have. It's been pretty frustrating, actually. I'll read the same student response three or four times and still not know what score to give it. And even simple choices, like... which lab supplies to order for the next unit, they can just stall me for an hour. I just can't seem to focus or make a decision.
Have you been feeling worthless or like you've been letting people down?

Yeah, I have. It's like... if a lesson goes badly, or even if a student just looks confused, I immediately take it as proof that I'm letting everyone down. I just keep replaying it in my head, feeling like I'm a terrible teacher, and honestly, a terrible mother, too. It's just this constant feeling that I'm failing at both.
Have these symptoms been going on nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah, definitely longer than two weeks. It's actually been going on for about a year and seven months now. It started right around the time I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my regular teaching load, and it's been pretty much every day since then.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge most days?
No, not really. I mean, I don't feel nervous or on edge, it's more just... heavy. Like I'm just dragging through the day, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious.

Before this started a year and seven months ago, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt this same kind of loss of interest, exhaustion, poor sleep, trouble concentrating, and self-critical thoughts for at least two weeks?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've had stressful times before, but nothing like this. This is the first time I've ever felt this way for this long.
Have these symptoms started to interfere with your work or your responsibilities at home?

Yes, it definitely has. I'm falling behind on my grading and lesson planning, and it's starting to actually affect my classroom. I even made a grading mistake recently that really scared me, because I used to be so meticulous about that kind of thing. And outside of work... I've pretty much stopped showing up for my friends and family the way I used to. My whole life has basically narrowed down to just barely getting through the school day, and then going home completely exhausted.
Do these symptoms feel stronger than what you’d normally expect from the extra work stress?

Yes, definitely. I mean, I've been teaching for a while now, so I know what normal work stress feels like. There are always busy times and extra workload. But this... it just feels completely different. It's a lot heavier than that, and I've never reacted to a heavy workload like this before. It doesn't feel like it's just about the work.
